title: Building Patterns
summary: Combine loops with variables to draw patterns, shapes, and repeating designs.

content.title: Loops Make Art
content.summary: Run the same `print` statement many times and you get a repeating pattern.
content.body: Loops are great for patterns. Run the same `print` statement many times and you get a design:
content.note:
**Output:**
```
* * *
* * *
* * *
* * *
* * *
```

Five identical rows — written with only two lines of code.

content.title: Growing Patterns with `i`
content.summary: Multiply a string by `i` to make each row longer as the loop counts up.
content.body:
Python can **multiply text** by a number to repeat it. `"#" * 3` gives you `"###"`.

When you put `i` inside the multiplication, each row can be different:
content.codeBlock:
for i in range(1, 6):
    print("#" * i)
content.note:
**Output:**
```
#
##
###
####
#####
```

`"#" * i` repeats the `#` character `i` times. As `i` grows, the row gets longer.

content.title: Mixing Text and `i`
content.summary: Combine a label with a growing pattern to create level-up style displays.
content.body: You can mix fixed text with the counter to label each row:
content.codeBlock:
for i in range(1, 4):
    print("Level", i, ":", "*" * i)
content.note:
**Output:**
```
Level 1 : *
Level 2 : **
Level 3 : ***
```

Each line has the level number and a growing row of stars.

content.title: Your Turn to Design
content.summary: There is no single right answer — experiment with different characters and ranges.
content.body:
Pattern ideas to try:

• A staircase of dashes: `"-" * i`
• A triangle of dots: `"." * i`
• A shrinking bar: `"#" * (10 - i)`
• A scoreboard with rows labeled `Round 1`, `Round 2`...

There is no single right answer — experiment and see what appears!

steps.instruction: Step 1: Write a `for` loop that runs 5 times. Use `range(1, 6)` so `i` goes from 1 to 5. Inside the loop, just print `i` for now — you should see the numbers 1 through 5.
steps.starterCode:
# Draw a growing triangle of stars
# Row 1: *
# Row 2: **
# Row 3: ***
# Row 4: ****
# Row 5: *****

steps.instruction: Step 2: Now change the loop body from `print(i)` to `print("*" * i)`. Each row should show that many stars.

bonusSteps.instruction: Bonus: After the growing triangle, add a **second** loop that makes the triangle shrink from 5 stars back to 1. Together they form a diamond shape!

progressiveHints: Step 2: replace `print(i)` with `print("*" * i)` — repeats `*` exactly `i` times.
